tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

The default daemon can keep many tabs and visit many sites; browser-use has
no per-site, screenshot, or result-count limit that requires a new daemon.
Chrome memory and page complexity are th… [truncated]

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

#### INGEST-PLAN
# Flint ingest plan: getting Drive into Flint over time

Status: approved 2026-10-13 (decisions 1 and 2 in section 9). Open items: the recount in step 0. Read with `docs/PLAN.md` (phases) and `docs/QUEUE.md` (named books and their order). This file adds the parts those do not cover: how the Drive grows, how much each step costs, who approves what, and how sub-agents are used.

## 1. The problem

Eric's Drive is large and still growing. The Sept 29 manifest counted 62,072 files (544 GB). After removing duplicates, 29,750 files (229 GB) are unique. Most are video (7,266 files, 151 GB) or papers and books (9,493 files, 28 GB). Only a small share can be read in full by an agent. The plan has to decide what to read, what to only index, and what to skip, and it has to keep doing that as new files arrive.

**Numbers conflict.** The Oct 12 build plan cites 17,847 files, 11,644 unique and 187 GB. The Sept 29 manifest says 62,072, 29,750 and 229 GB. A fresh recount is the first task (step 0 below). No budget in this plan should be treated as final until that count is done.

## 2. Principles

1. **Tier before you read.** Every file gets one of three tiers. Only Tier A gets the full review gate.
   - **A, deep ingest:** a paper, book or deck that will be cited. Full gate.
   - **B, catalog only:** indexed by title and metadata, searchable, never atomized.
   - **C, skip:** not useful to Flint (logistics, duplicates, forms, personal files).
2. **Gate what gets cited.** Nothing reaches the vault without the review gate in `docs/PLAN.md` and the AGENTS.md conventions. The gate is expensive, so it runs only on Tier A.
3. **Small batches, approved in short sittings.** Eric approves candidates in batches of at most 10. Approval is the only human step that cannot be automated.
4. **Model tier by job.** Deterministic code for catalog, dedup and text extraction (no tokens). Haiku for triage and labelling. Opus for atomizing and reviewing. Never Haiku for atomizing (ingest-book rule).
5. **Never ingest athlete data.** DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult exports and PFF exports stay out of the catalog. W13 stays held. This rule is checked at catalog time, at compile time and in any test set.
6. **Drive is the source of truth. The repo holds only pointers and summaries.** Source PDFs and video never go into git (AGENTS.md: files over 95 MB never go in git).

## 3. The pipeline

| Stage | What happens | Who or what | Cost | Exit criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Catalog (monthly) | Walk Drive roots, record new and changed files since the last manifest, dedup by md5 | `scripts/build_manifest.ps1` (Windows) or Mac equivalent | No tokens | Manifest updated, counts reported in STATUS |
| 1. Triage (weekly, for new files) | Rules pass, then model pass on unclassified files; assign discipline and tier | `scripts/triage_rules.py`, then Haiku or the chosen classifier | Low | Every new unique file has a discipline and a tier |
| 2. Shortlist (weekly) | Tier A candidates grouped by discipline, at most 10 per sitting | Flint, labelled without the classifier | Low | Shortlist file in `docs/shortlists/` |
| 3. Approve | Eric approves, edits or rejects each candidate | **Eric** | Eric's time | Each candidate marked approved, edited or dropped |

**Started 2026-10-22 (Mac, Opus).** All earlier Drive dedup was names-only (the mount hangs). The Drive API
gives an `md5Checksum` for every binary file, so one API listing answers all three asks: find, dedupe, rename.

**Tool:** `~/DEV/_INBOX/tools/drive_index.py` (read-only; never moves or deletes). Index and CSVs in
`~/DEV/_INBOX/drive-index/` (gitignored; `summary.md` holds counts only). `DexaProject` is never stored.

```bash
cd ~/DEV/_INBOX
python3 -I tools/drive_index.py find gps weekly      # best-placed copy first, + link; --all shows backups
python3 -I tools/drive_index.py build                # re-list Drive (~15 min, 1,337 API pages)
python3 -I tools/drive_index.py report               # CSVs + summary.md
```

**First run (07:10, 614,290 items).** Every file gets a zone. Reports:
- `delete_candidates.csv` — files in `_PARKED_COPIES` (102,413 / 116 GB) and `99_UNSORTED` (4,147 / 56 GB)
  with a **byte-identical** twin in a kept folder. This is the evidence the delete wave needs.
- `dupes_in_browsed_folders.csv` — 16,865 groups (46,585 files, 76 GB extra) duplicated inside folders Eric browses.
- `backup_folders.csv` — 113 backup-looking folders outside `_MACHINE`. Review list; has false hits (`TB's Training Info (snapshot …)`, `From Landon`).
- `naming_problems.csv` — 549 in `03_REPORTS`, `06_TEMPLATES` and top folders (324 reports not date-first, 226 spaces, 141 two-digit seasons).
- Google Docs/Sheets (701) have no checksum: never called duplicates.

**Found:** 214,368 files (36 GB) had no path. **Mostly "Computers" backups** (old Backup and Sync device roots such
as `My Laptop (2)`, outside My Drive; one holds a copy of the Drive folder itself), filed now as zone `computers`.
Some `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy` files were also unplaced: unordered paging likely skipped a few folders. The build now
pages by `createdTime` and runs a repair pass that fetches skipped ancestors; its printed count separates the two.
**Also:** `99_UNSORTED` is 76 GB, not the 23.8 GB the FUSE scan showed (`From_REMOTE_DESK` alone 55 GB, 95% exact
twins). The "leave until 2027-01-01" call was made on the small number. **The rebuild with that fix was stopped by Claude Code at page
1,300/1,337 because the Mac was low on memory.** Build now keeps small tuples instead of API dicts.

- [ ] **NEXT 1:** rerun `build` then `report` (memory free first). Read the new `computers` numbers.
- [ ] **NEXT 2 (Eric):** delete wave, **by folder, not by file** (102k single trash calls is ~14 h). A folder at
  ~100% twins gets one trash call; a folder below that has its unique files moved out first, then is trashed.
  Re-check the twins exist at the moment of trashing. Drive trash keeps 30 days. One folder per sitting.
  **Gate before anything under `Computers/`:** open Drive for desktop preferences on the Mac **and** the Windows
  laptop (back in use since 10-21) and confirm no folder backs up to "My Laptop". Turn it off, wait one scan.
  Trashing a live backup's cloud copy is re-uploaded (Backup mode) or **deletes the local files** (Mirror mode).

# Flint ingest queue

The order in which sources go into the vault library. Each course or book is atomized
by Sonnet into `staging/library/` and reviewed by Codex against its source, following
the ingest review gate. Only then is it copied into SecondBrain, indexed and committed.

## Promoted to the vault

- **Harries, The Fundamentals of On-Field Rehabilitation**: 33 entries, domain `rehab-and-return-to-play`. SecondBrain `c15460d` (2026-09-26), after two review rounds by an independent Opus reviewer (Codex was capped) and nine reciprocal links. Harries batch 2 is pending: 5 items the first pass missed (the case-review template, fitting rehab into the team week, the HSR format progression, the mid-rehab hamstring checkpoint, and speed prescription in late rehab).
- **2026-09-27, SecondBrain `aacbccd`:** Harries batch 2 (+4, now 37); Old Bull course (37, new domain `performance-technology-and-leadership`); Issurin *Block Periodization* Ch1-3 (28); Bondarchuk *Transfer of Training* I Ch1-2 (20); *Supertraining* Ch1-3 (113); Landon Evans *Elite Sports Performance* lectures (34). Every source went through independent Opus falsification reviews, with a round 2 where fixes were heavy. Resume points: *Supertraining* Ch4, Issurin Ch4, Bondarchuk I Ch3.

## In progress

1. (promoted, see above) **Harries**.
   - Domain: new `rehab-and-return-to-play`. Book slug: `on-field-rtp--harries`.
   - Stance: Eric's 2026-09-25 review. Keep it as a dosage reference; the theory is Taberner's control-chaos continuum with a velocity layer.
2. **Old Bull Performance course**.
   - Domain: new `performance-technology-and-leadership`. Book slug: `old-bull-performance-course--old-bull`.

## Staged, not yet atomized: 42 Analytics (2026-10-01)

128 SSAC talk sources staged at `staging/sources/42analytics/` (local). The 23 `supported` talks are atomized (152 entries, `staging/library/sports-analytics-and-decision-making/ssac-talks--42analytics/`), sample-reviewed and fixed, then a second full round (r4a/r4b, 2026-10-02) and a Codex falsify round; **promoted 2026-10-02 (SecondBrain `88acfc0`, fixes `ad006ad`, merge `aa41109`: 151 entries). Gate closed.** See `docs/intake-42analytics.md`.

## Next: Landon Evans (queued 2026-09-26 by Eric)

681 unique files. Most of it is a curated library Landon gave Eric (`From Landon Evans/Eric Files/`), not Landon's own writing. Landon's own teaching goes first, because it is his voice that gets compared with Eric's method.

| Step | What | Files | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | His *Elite Sports Performance* course: Units 1 to 4 lecture slides, plus the fuller Evans Unit 3 set (lectures 1 to 8, with an exam study guide) | about 30 PDFs | Atomize as a course (`elite-sports-performance--evans`). The slides are text but sparse (22 to 45 words a page), so slide-only entries are capped at `untested` |
| L2 | His talks: CVASPS "Physical Preparation in the NCAA: A Complementary Approach" (1 GB video, plus a CVASPS mp3), and the 2014 Boston "Performance Analytics" slides | 3 | Transcribe the CVASPS talk first in the transcription queue. Where the talk matches an L1 entry, raise that entry to `supported` |
| L3 | Therapy folder: fills the rehab gap next to Harries | 46 papers, 17 videos, 3 audio | Papers go to Zotero; video and audio go to the transcription queue |
| L4 | Training books (Verkhoshansky, Bondarchuk, Issurin, Zatsiorsky, Siff, Francis, and others) | 188 flagged as books | `ingest-book`, one at a time behind the gate. **First: *Supertraining*, started 2026-09-26 at Eric's call.** Source is the 6th Expanded single PDF from TB (591 pages, text, md5-verified), slug `supertraining--verkhoshansky`, domain strength-and-conditioning. Chapter map plus Chapter 1 are in progress; later chapters run one batch each. **Then Bondarchuk (queued by Eric 2026-09-26)**, in the order below |
| L5 | Papers in Physical Preparation, Science and Training Science | about 350 | Bulk import into Zotero, deduplicated against the library |
| L6 | Nutrition | 242 | Later. It is outside the current synthesis order |
| V8 | Short articles: Block Training System (endurance, 3 papers), Maximal Strength Training in Speed-Strength Sports, Quickness and Velocity in Sports Movements, Natalia Verkhoshansky's *Jump Training 101* | Golden CCCE, TB, AP Topics/Jumps | small | Text | Bundle |

## Wave 1: approved tier-A shortlists (Eric, 2026-09-29)

Eric approved all 14 discipline shortlists in `docs/shortlists/` as a first wave: "there is a lot more to add however, as a first wave this is good." This wave holds 84 of the 97 tier-A files; the other 13 are already queued above or in the vault. Wave 2 will come from Eric's additions and the candidate pass on the rule-classified files (decision 5 in `docs/shortlists/README.md`).

- **Progress (2026-10-10):** through the gate and waiting on Eric's promotion approval: W7-W10, W18, W19 (2026-10-09) and W20, W21, W22, W24, W25, W27, W28, W29 (2026-10-10). Held for Eric: W13 (athlete data), W16, W17, W23 (identity). Over the cloud connector's size limit: W1-W5, W11, W12, W15, W26, W31, W32. W21's venue is CSCCa 2018 (printed), not CVASPS. See `docs/STATUS.md`.
- **Order (Eric, decision 3):** the whole wave goes after the queue above (Supertraining Ch4-9, Bondarchuk, Zatsiorsky, Issurin, Francis, Verkhoshansky). Inside the wave, cheap items come first: decks and lectures to atomize, then recordings to transcribe, then books. Within each route the order follows PLAN Phase 4: rehab and RTP, speed, strength, conditioning, load monitoring, recovery, nutrition, then the rest.
- **Books:** 30 books at 1 to 3 sessions each is the bottleneck. Take two or three per discipline at a time, not all 30 in a row.
- **Papers already in Zotero (decision 2, left to Claude):** they get a Paper Brief through the Zotero queue, not an atomize pass. That pipeline already exists, and atomizing them would duplicate it. Eric can overrule.
- **Mike Golden (decision 4):** the library as a whole does not get TB or Landon priority. The Golden files below were approved one by one on their own merit (decision 1), and *Blueprint for Success* stays (decision 6).
- **Vertical Foundations (W60):** author is Joel Smith (Eric, 2026-09-29).
- Paths are relative to each Source root, as in the shortlists.
| W84 | already in Zotero | ACL injury meta-analysis in female athletes | Injury risk and prevention | 04_RESEARCH | `_INBOX/drive-zotero-import_2026-06/pdfs-pass3/1T6uyno4gWOiF-yf7JHU7DfxkkGCCnKpr.pdf` | 9 |

## Wave 2: Jev pass additions (approved by Eric, 2026-09-29)

From the decision-5 candidate pass (`docs/jev-pass-2026-09-29.md`). Goes after Wave 1. The three papers go to Zotero first, then get a Paper Brief through the Zotero queue (decision 2); the book goes through `ingest-book` behind the gate.

| X2 | paper to Zotero | Gabbett and Oetter 2024, Sports Medicine, "From Tissue to System": what constitutes an appropriate response to loading | Injury risk and prevention | 01_PROJECTS | `_ACTIVE/2023-09-12_SportScienceResearchRepo/SourcePapers/From Tissue to System - What Constitutes an Appropriate Response to Loading.pdf` | |
| X3 | paper to Zotero | Mueller-Wohlfahrt et al. 2012, BJSM, Munich consensus on terminology and classification of muscle injuries | Injury risk and prevention | 05_SYSTEMS | `TMG/TMG Library/TMG/Br J Sports Med-2012-Mueller-Wohlfahrt-bjsports-2012-091448.pdf` | |
| X4 | book | *Advances in Functional Training* (Inference: Michael Boyle, from the folder name) | Periodization and programming; Rehab and return to play | TB Training Info | `Boyle/Advances in Functional Training.pdf` | 159 |
| X5 | book | *The Black Book of Training Secrets*, **Enhanced Edition**, Christian Thibaudeau (F. Lepine Publishing). Practitioner text, not peer-reviewed. Approved by Eric 2026-10-03, Enhanced Edition by his choice | Strength and power; Periodization and programming | TB Training Info | `Christian Thibaudeau/Christian Thibaudeau - Black Book of Trainings Secrets (Enhanced Edition).pdf` (md5 `7c06e9d9…`; local: `09_PRO_DEV/TB's Training Info (snapshot 2026-09-26)/`) | 251 |

- "The System" = *The System: Soviet Periodization Adapted for the American Strength Coach*, Johnny Parker, Al Miller, Rob Panariello with Jeremy Hall (On Target Publications, 2018), 385 pp, ~1,665 text chars/page. **Already queued as W62**; no new row. Two byte-different copies exist (md5 `7c8eebb6…`, the W62 path, and `7e743c19…` in `00_INBOX` / TB Training Info); same book.

## What "done in 7 days" means

Flint will not hold the whole Drive in 7 days. Most of the Drive stays catalog-only, by design
(INGEST-PLAN section 8). "Done" means **Flint v1 is complete and runs on a weekly cadence**:

1. The catalog is true again (roots re-pointed after the 10/14 and 10/22 Drive moves, counts in STATUS).

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Vault library | 1,760 entries, 24 books/decks. Promote dry run on all 24: **0 new files waiting**. The "promotion backlog" in older STATUS entries is closed. |
| Shortlist | **Approved 2026-09-29** (QUEUE.md Wave 1 + Wave 2). INGEST-PLAN step 3 is stale. |
| Wave 1 left | 11 large decks never run (W1-W5, W11, W12, W15, W26, W31, W32; were too big for the cloud connector, fine on the Mac). W13 held (athlete data). W16, W17 held (identity check). |

| Recordings | 21 approved, 0 transcribed. `scripts/transcribe.py` exists (faster-whisper via `uv`). |
| Papers | 3 to Zotero (X1-X3), 3 already there. |
| Interview | Prep done (`docs/interview-prep.md`); session not held. |
| Synthesis | 1 note exists (peaking and taper). Rehab/RTP not started. |
| Catalog roots | `config/roots.json` is stale. Folders moved on 10/14; TB snapshot, AP & Sports Science and RTP Clinic no longer match by name. |
| Drive index | Built 07:10 today, 614k items. **Now stale**: Grok moved 3,699 files at 11:09. |

- Installed 10/21 (`~/Downloads/Grok_Bot_0.72.1.dmg`).
- Made Drive folder `_TO_REVIEW` (id `1Hx7wGpZZ2hFLdybZ73UWBC9UGEaGZo8-`) at the Drive root on 10/21.
- Today 11:09 it moved **3,699 duplicate files (50.4 GB)** into `_TO_REVIEW`. Moves only, nothing trashed.
  Log: `data/drive_dedupe_2026-10-22/move_log.csv` (status `moved` for all 3,699); plan: `dup_plan.csv`.
- It picked the kept copy with Flint's root priorities. 1,985 moves came from
  `04_RESEARCH/_INBOX/drive-zotero-import_2026-06`, 682 from `From_REMOTE_DESK`, 358 from `10_ARCHIVE`.
- Checked: no DexaProject or `_MACHINE` files moved. Four Flint queue paths now point at a moved copy;
  each has a byte-identical twin that stayed, so no content is lost.

**Lanes (one writer per folder per sitting):**

| Agent | Owns | Never |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Drive index, reports, Flint roots, Flint queue and gate, trash calls after Eric says yes | Moves files Grok is working on |
| Grok | Duplicate moves into `_TO_REVIEW` only, with a move log | Trashes; touches `_MACHINE`, `DexaProject`, `Football/` pipelines, `Computers` |
| Eric | Says yes to each trash wave and each promotion | |

Grok's exact job is not written down yet. Eric confirms the lane above (question at the end).

## Day by day

Each day: one Eric sitting of about 20 minutes, the rest runs in the background.

| Day | Drive (ongoing org) | Flint (ingest) | Eric |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Thu 10/22** | Rebuild the index after the Grok moves: `cd ~/DEV/_INBOX && python3 -I tools/drive_index.py build && python3 -I tools/drive_index.py report` (close apps first; the last run stopped on low memory) | Re-point `config/roots.json` to current paths. Recount Flint roots from `drive.sqlite`. Write the true counts in STATUS (closes INGEST-PLAN step 0) | Read this plan. Answer the two questions at the end |
| **Fri 10/23** | Computers gate: on the Mac **and** the Windows laptop, open Drive for desktop preferences, confirm nothing backs up to "My Laptop" | Start the overnight transcription queue: 21 recordings, Darren Burgess and CVASPS first. Mac only, no tokens | Computers gate (5 min) |
| **Sat 10/24** | Game day. Nothing | Transcription runs | None |
| **Sun 10/25** | Trash wave 1: `_TO_REVIEW` (50 GB). Re-check each twin exists at trash time. One folder, one trash call | Papers X1-X3 to Zotero. Gate: Wave 1 decks batch A (W1-W5) | Yes/no on trash wave 1. W16/W17 identity (5 min) |
| **Mon 10/26** | Trash wave 2: `_PARKED/OneDrive-Import/XX_MIGRATION/From_REMOTE_DESK` (96% twins, 65 GB). Move the 4% unique files out first | `/interview-me` session (45 min). Gate: decks batch B (W11, W12, W15) | Interview |
| **Tue 10/27** | Trash wave 3: `99_UNSORTED/From_REMOTE_DESK` (95%, 54 GB). **Only after** Flint roots no longer point there | Fold interview into baseline v1. Gate: decks batch C (W26, W31, W32). Atomize the first transcripts | Promotion yes/no for batches A-C |
| **Wed 10/28** | Naming: rename the 549 permanent-tier files by `gws drive files update` (IDs and links stay), from an approved list | Write synthesis note 1: Rehab and RTP. Add the weekly and monthly cadence to `weekly-review` | Approve rename list. Read the synthesis note and answer its questions |

## After this week (ongoing)

- **Weekly (Fri, in `weekly-review`, 20 min):** index rebuild + report; one trash wave (next folder from the
  Task 8 per-folder table, biggest twin share first); up to 10 new Flint candidates; 2 to 3 books through the gate.
- **Monthly:** Flint catalog recount from the Drive index (the Mac replaces `build_manifest.ps1`).
- **Season end:** Task 4 (Area folders). Nothing under `Football/` or live pipelines moves before then.
- **Later:** the classifier comparison (rules vs Haiku vs Jev). It is not needed this week; the shortlist is approved.

## Rules that do not bend this week

- Trash by folder, one per sitting, twins re-checked at trash time. Drive trash keeps 30 days.
- Nothing under `Computers/` until the gate on both machines is done.
- DexaProject, Catapult, PFF and athlete exports never enter the catalog or the vault. W13 stays out.
- Papers go to Zotero, never through the atomizer.
- Nothing reaches the vault without the gate and Eric's yes.

## Cost

| Work | Opus calls |
|---|---|
| 11 Wave 1 decks (3 batches, about 5 calls per deck) | about 55 |
| Interview fold + synthesis note | about 8 |
| Index, recount, transcription, Zotero, trash, renames | 0 (scripts) |
| **Total** | **about 63** |

The approved ceiling is 15 Opus calls a week (INGEST-PLAN decision 2). Eric decides below.

## Questions for Eric

1. **Opus ceiling for this week.**
   - **A. Keep 15.** This week: catalog, transcripts, papers, interview, synthesis start, one deck batch.
     The other decks finish in about 4 weeks.
   - **B. Lift to about 65 for this week only, then back to 15.** All 7 "done" items land by Wed 10/28.
   - Recommended: **B**. It is the only way to finish in 7 days, and the extra spend stops on Wed.
2. **Grok's job.** What is Grok set to do, and where can it write? Default if no answer: the lane in the
   table above (moves into `_TO_REVIEW` only, never trashes), and Claude does not touch `_TO_REVIEW`
   until Eric says the Grok run is finished.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Flint

## What this is
Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. This repo builds the knowledge base behind that role. It catalogs Eric's
Drive (his own material, TB's Training Info, Landon Evans, courses, papers), routes the
high-value sources into Zotero and the SecondBrain vault, and writes per-discipline
synthesis notes that compare the sources against Eric's own method. It is a side-lane
project, outside the prioritization-slate cap. See `README.md` for the approach and
`docs/PLAN.md` for the checklist.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- `data/` is gitignored except aggregate summaries. Regenerate the file-level manifest with `pwsh scripts/build_manifest.ps1`.
- Codex workers read staged copies in `staging/`, never the Drive root. DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued.
- The ingest review gate has two stages.
  1. Before atomizing, verify the source artifact by an independent route: page order, scanned versus text, transcripts checked against captions.
  2. Before promoting, Codex reviews the staged entries against the staged sources, with instructions to falsify (`staging/review_<source>_codex.md`). Nothing reaches the vault without a GO or a GO AFTER FIXES that has been applied.
- Library entries label every voice. The source author's statements are plain. Eric's judgments get "Eric's review:". The entry writer's own reasoning gets "Inference:". No unlabeled judgments. Every number carries a timestamp or page the reviewer can check, and a claim is only tagged "confirmed in PDF" if that PDF is staged. (Learned from the Harries review, 2026-09-26: 25 of 35 files needed fixes, mostly for attribution.)
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
